Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary You are leading an expanding Empire. You must choose the path that will get you to develop faster and better than your competitors. Contents 1 Playing 2 Drafting 3 Planning 4 Production 5 End of round 6 Scoring Playing It's a Wonderful World is played in 4 rounds with three phases each: first Drafting, then Planning, and finally Production. Drafting In a 3+ player game, 7 cards are dealt to each player. In a 2 player game 10 cards are dealt instead. All players simultaneously draft a single card from their hand and then reveal them. Remaining cards are passed and drafting repeats until 7 cards are drafted by each player (in a 2 player game some cards will be left over). Planning Then players will choose which drafted cards to: keep for building and which to recycle (discard) for cubes (shown bottom-right). Cubes gained are placed onto kept cards to pay for their building cost (upper-left) or on starting Empire card where 5 will immediately be converted to a single red (wild) cube to be used on demand. Non-red cubes on the starting card may only be used to make a red cube. When all costs are paid the card may be added into player's Empire tableau (tokens on card are discarded) and any bonus (if any shown bottom-middle of image above the bottom bar) is gained to player's Empire card. Note that any incomplete card may be discarded to gain its recycle cube to your Empire card at any time. Resource cube placed on a recycled card are returned to the supply. Production Each production phase is sequence grey, black, green, yellow, and finally blue cube production sectors. Each of those productions have three parts. 1. produce cubes of a color - each player produces cubes of current color according to what is shown in the bottom bar of cards in Empire tableau. 2. award highest production - single player with the highest production of current color gains one character token (each with 1 vp) matching the icon shown for that sector. Blue Financier for grey/yellow, red General for black/blue, and winning player's choice for green. 3. place cubes - as during drafting cubes are placed on incomplete cards and completed cards may immediately be built and added to Empire tableau. Sector production is repeated for each color ending with blue which ends the round. End of round Incomplete cards remain. If not round 4, each player gets new set of cards to restart drafting but passing in the opposite player order. Scoring Besides 1 point per character token, many cards have some victory points in lower left corner. Some score by other types of cards added to Empire (see bottom-right icons). The player with the most points wins. Ties broken by having most Empire cards and then most character tokens. In It’s a Wonderful World, you are an expanding Empire and must choose your path to your future. You must develop faster and better than your competitors. You’ll carefully plan your expansion to develop your production power and rule over this new world.

It’s a Wonderful World is a cards drafting and engine building game from 1 to 5 players. Each round, players will draft 7 cards and then choose which ones will be recycled to immediately acquire Resources, and which ones will be kept for construction to produce Resources each round and/or gain victory points.

When a card is fully built, it’s added to the player’s Empire to increase the player’s production capacity for each round. The mechanical twist being that the production phase works in a specific order. You'll have to plan your constructions carefully!

For a deeper insight of the gameplay, please follow this link : It's a Wonderful World - First steps

In addition to the base game, players can also enjoy expansions boxes introducing an innovative Campaign mode. Each Campaign offers a storyline to follow and many gameplay twists. At the end of each campaign, players will open a reward booster to unlock new cards, enhance their base game and keep a memory of what happened during the campaign. All the campaigns can be replayed and don’t imply game components destruction.

More info on the Campaign mode : It's a Wonderful World - Campaign Mode 

—description from the publisher
community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Uninspired cube pusher. Pasted on theme that literally could be anything. Splendor has more theme and is more fun than this and its five years older. This "game" is devoid of all fun. Here are the rules of the game: Build buildings that produce cubes that let you build more buildings that produce more cubes that let you build buildings that give victory points. I don't get what is interesting about this. If thats your thing there are way better engine builders out there, you may as well just play 7 Wonders, Gizmos, or res arcana.

[Rating: 1/10] My rating of 1 is somewhat vindictive honestly, I’d probably play this again if it came up. But the total banality of it is just so depressing. It’s so totally mechanical. They could have made some effort to make this thing interesting in any numbers of ways, but it’s just a cube fiddler extraordinaire.

[Rating: 1/10] Drafting, engine builder but it runs 90 mins=boo.  Higher if shorter but really for drafting quick games Sushi-Go (15 mins), 7Wonders (30-45) and engine building->Splendor. + The timing mechanic was good + You can hate draft and use cards for resources   - For a cube pusher it is simply too long  - Shallow decision making  - Good helping of random draw.

[Rating: 1/10] Easy game to take a break from complex game Have interesting mechanic: Sidebar convenient to read resource production which I will not be able to use because printing and cutting cards are a havoc I will still buy it because it is cheap and most probably I will use it for gaming instead Note: Some of your seen price might be the expansion packs especially this game Resource managements so JH might dislike it and I should probably take a break from it

[Rating: 1/10] Pure engine building, mechanics distilled to the point that they suck the soul out of the game. "Going through the motions" would be an understatement. It is presented that there are various pathways you can explore (i.e., different elements/colors to focus heavily on, or whatever they're called) but each of those paths feels eerily similar. Would need to play this more to get a stronger and/or more accurate opinion on it, but after about 5 or 6 plays, I'm not itching to continue.

[Rating: 1/10] Very nice blend of drafting and engine building in a tight quick game. I regret getting the KS edition cause the box is way too big for such a small game that I rarely bring it to game night for that reason. Unfortunately needs the expansion to fix the luck of the draw and dominant strategies of the base game.  It's one of the better drafting games with the expansion, but even then it's still pretty boring with how the game leans too much into the obvious synergies between the colors.

[Rating: 2/10] I HATED this game. I would have hated this game a decade ago. Games have gotten a lot better since then. It's everything I don't like. Dry resource conversion in a convoluted way for dry points with no theme. They seemed to like it. I will never play this again. If my option was play this or go home, I'm going home.   :soblue: Dry resource conversion :soblue: Convoluted resource system :soblue: Dry points and no theme

[Rating: 2/10] I was thinking really hard about the rating I'm going to give this game and it just has to be a 2, because "very bad - won’t play ever again" is the only description that fits what I think about it. It's a dull, boring and uninspired engine builder with a negative fun factor. I felt like I didn't make a single interesting decision throughout the entire game, it's all about tedious cube manipulation. Do yourself a favour and pick ANY other drafting/engine building game from the BGG's top 200. Why does this game get so much love from the community? What am I missing?

[Rating: 2/10] Okay but not worth keeping in collection. Feels like trading cubes for cubes and the theme feels pasted on. I’d play it if offered, but would almost always prefer something else. Pretty good engine building. Don’t really like drafting games. Each play felt about the same to me. Will be selling after only a couple of plays.
